audit.why: 51.7% over 1849 games supports EVEN 5.5/10. Veigar has no mobility whatsoever and one defensive tool on a 20s cooldown at rank 1; Lissandra's problem is the 1000-range Q and the infinite AP stacking, not the duel.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows disagreed across layers. phases[N].side read Skill, Lissandra, Lissandra, Skill, Lissandra, Skill, Veigar while content win[N] read Lissandra, Skill, Skill, Lissandra, Lissandra, Lissandra, Lissandra — which is exactly packet.levelChart.
audit.why: Level 1 Veigar has no Event Horizon and a shorter effective trade, so it is Lissandra's. Levels 2-3 the cage arrives on a 20s cooldown and answers the claw, so those are skill. From 4 the claw is up often enough to punish a champion with zero mobility, and from 6 the untargetable self-cast blanks Primordial Burst.
audit.corrected: All six sides moved onto the content values, with every why rewritten in the same proposal where it no longer matched.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer puts the cage on the wrong ability slot twice: spikes[0].text says 'his W stun-cage' and wants.you[1] says 'blink out of his W cage'. Event Horizon is his E; W is Dark Matter, a delayed area hit. spikes[1].text and mid also claim your R 'hard-cancels his Primordial Burst execute' — Primordial Burst is a targeted blast, not a channel. breakdown.cooldowns held no digit.
audit.why: Riot's text: Event Horizon 'creates a cage that Stuns enemies that pass through' (E, 20/18.5/17/15.5/14, 725 range); Dark Matter 'calls a great mass of dark matter to fall from the sky' (W); Primordial Burst 'Blasts target enemy champion' (R, 120/90/60). What actually beats Primordial Burst is Frozen Tomb's self-cast, which makes Lissandra untargetable and invulnerable — a targeted blast then has nothing to hit.
audit.corrected: Cage moved back to E throughout, the cancel claim replaced with the untargetable interaction, and real cooldowns written into breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim under 'Self-R the all-in and counter-burst'; dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim under 'Tomb him while his burst is already spent'. dontsFull[0].d was a name-swappable template.
audit.corrected: Rewritten using the untargetable self-cast, the 120s Primordial Burst and Baleful Strike's 1000 range.

edits.before: Q-shatter the wave and chip his melee step-ups — your early Q harass is better than the lane gives it credit for.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours: Ice Shard at 725 trades better than Baleful Strike and he has no Event Horizon to punish you with yet.

edits.before: W online: anyone who closes onto you eats a root. The anti-engage layer is already real at level 2.
edits.after: Even at 2 — your W roots inside 450, but Veigar never has to come closer than his 1000-range Q.

edits.before: E claw completes the kit — you now have the lane's strangest engage and a guaranteed exit. Greed carefully; the claw is slow.
edits.after: Skill at 3: Event Horizon is 20s at rank 1 and stuns anything crossing its edge, so his cage answers your claw as often as not.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q spam stops hurting your mana. Chip Veigar every time he touches the wave.
edits.after: Lost Chapter steadies your mana, and you can claw out of the cage to punish the most immobile mage alive.

edits.before: - Veigar Event Horizon (Cage): matchup-defining — Only the cage EDGE stuns — hold position near the center or leave before it forms; never dash into the wall. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget R Frozen Tomb (self-cast) for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Event Horizon is 20s at rank 1 and 14s at rank 5, and only the EDGE stuns — stand near the centre or leave before it forms, and never claw through the wall. - Baleful Strike is 6s at rank 1 and 4s at rank 5 from 1000 range. - Primordial Burst is 120s at rank 1.

edits.before: Veigar wins by landing Event Horizon (Cage), denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Veigar wins by catching you on the edge of Event Horizon, then stacking Phenomenal Evil until one Primordial Burst is lethal.

edits.before: Q-shatter his wave contact, and when he steps to punish, W-root into full rotation and walk — the root tax makes every aggressive step expensive.
edits.after: Q him at 725 whenever he steps up to last-hit with Baleful Strike, and if he walks inside 450, W-root him — he has no dash at all to leave with.

edits.before: Clawing in with W on cooldown 'to poke' — an engage tool spent on chip damage is a Lissandra standing in melee range with no ice left.
edits.after: Clawing through the edge of Event Horizon — the wall stuns anything that crosses it, and you land inside his cage with no exit left.

edits.before: Good trade: Q-shatter his wave contact, and when he steps to punish, W-root into full rotation and walk — the root tax makes every aggressive step expensive. Bad trade: Clawing in with W on cooldown 'to poke' — an engage tool spent on chip damage is a Lissandra standing in melee range with no ice left.
edits.after: Good trade: Q him at 725 whenever he steps up to last-hit with Baleful Strike, and if he walks inside 450, W-root him — he has no dash at all. Bad trade: clawing through the edge of Event Horizon, where the wall stuns anything that crosses it and you land inside his cage with no exit for 24s.

edits.before: Carry through picks — claw-root-tomb converts vision into kills better than any control mage; the map shrinks every time your E is up.
edits.after: Carry by refusing the poke war — he stacks AP off every spell that hits you, so take the fight at 550 rather than trading Q for Q.

edits.before: Ahead, hunt: claw into every river skirmish first, tomb the carry, and snowball picks — Veigar farming under tower can't stop a roaming Lissandra.
edits.after: Ahead, hunt: he is completely immobile behind a 20s cage, so claw in the moment Event Horizon is down, tomb him, and starve the AP stacks.

edits.before: Q-shatter his wave contact, and when he steps to punish, W-root into full rotation and walk — the root tax makes every aggressive step expensive.
edits.after: Self-R as Primordial Burst comes — untargetable and invulnerable means the blast finds nothing, then W-root him and Q while he waits 120s.

edits.before: That is Veigar’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Baleful Strike reaches 1000 and returns every 4s at rank 5.

edits.before: Clawing in with W on cooldown 'to poke' — an engage tool spent on chip damage is a Lissandra standing in melee range with no ice left.
edits.after: With Event Horizon down and his R spent, Veigar is a 1000-range Q and nothing else — walk him down instead of paying a 120s tomb.

edits.before: You can dodge or E through his slow Baleful Strike Q and punish the long cast, but from 2-3 his W stun-cage and empowered Q let a good Veigar zone you if you facecheck carelessly.
edits.after: You can dodge or E around his slow Baleful Strike and punish the long cast, but from 2-3 his E cage and the delayed Dark Matter let a good Veigar zone you if you step in carelessly.

edits.before: Your R hard-cancels his Primordial Burst execute and, more importantly, you can E-flash or E-R engage before he lands his E cage, denying his entire combo.
edits.after: Your self-R goes untargetable, so Primordial Burst finds nothing, and you can E-flash or R him before he ever lands Event Horizon, denying the combo.

edits.before: From 4 onward your all-in threat flips the lane. Save E to dash out of Event Horizon or, better, E-in over the cage's outer ring so the stun never triggers, then Ice Shard him. At 6 your R cancels his ult execute and your engage range beats his combo setup — force him to play reactive.
edits.after: From 4 onward your all-in threat flips the lane. Save E to claw out of Event Horizon rather than through its edge, where the stun triggers, then Ice Shard him. At 6 your self-R goes untargetable, so Primordial Burst finds nothing, and your engage beats his combo setup — force him to play reactive.

edits.before: Hold E to blink out of his W cage before it stuns
edits.after: Hold E to blink out of his E cage before it stuns

notes: Six of seven chart rows disagreed across layers; I moved the full layer onto the content values, which match packet.levelChart, so no paired win[N] edit exists to write. phases[5].why and phases[6].why already described Lissandra winning and needed no rewrite; the other four were rewritten in the same proposal. The content layer had the cage on the wrong ability slot in two places (spikes[0].text and wants.you[1] said W; Event Horizon is E) and claimed Frozen Tomb 'cancels' Primordial Burst — it does not cancel a targeted blast, it makes you untargetable so the blast has no target. Veigar's W is listed with cd 0 in the kit because Phenomenal Evil reduces it; I cited no Dark Matter cooldown rather than write '0 seconds'. No lint findings on report[] and nothing there names a fabricated ability, so report[] was untouched — note that report[5].t and report[11].t still repeat the old cage-edge phrasing, which is correct as written.
